solutionSql:
SELECT s.customer_id,
       COUNT(*)::integer AS shipments,
       SUM(b.billed_amt) AS billed
FROM shipments s
LEFT JOIN (
  SELECT shipment_id, SUM(amount) AS billed_amt
  FROM invoices
  GROUP BY shipment_id
) b ON b.shipment_id = s.id
GROUP BY s.customer_id
ORDER BY s.customer_id;

rules.howSolved: Counted shipment rows with COUNT(*) over shipments, which includes shipments with no invoice.
Drove the query from shipments with a LEFT JOIN to pre-aggregated invoices, so a customer whose shipments are all unbilled still gets a row.
SUM over the pre-aggregated invoice totals returns NULL when a customer has no invoice rows.
Grouped shipments by customer_id, so only customers with at least one shipment appear.

notes: Invoice totals are pre-aggregated per shipment, so the shipment count stays exact even if a shipment had more than one invoice. The empty dataset has no invoices and returns billed NULL for each row. Row counts per dataset: sample=6, nulls=6, boundary=6, empty=6, precision=6. Ran on every listed dataset without error.
